visual_goal: Show one front end, one loyalty program and shared services above two distinct offer shapes, with some home bookings routed to a legacy checkout.
prompt: A top-to-bottom layered diagram. Top: three unlabeled generic traveler figures standing side by side, with one arrow down into a wide slab labeled 'One front end'. Beside that slab on the right, a small coin-and-key token labeled 'One Key loyalty' attached by one short arrow from the slab. Below, a wide slab labeled 'Shared services'. One arrow from 'One front end' down to 'Shared services'. From 'Shared services', the picture splits into two separate columns: left column a box with a grid of many identical rooms labeled 'Hotel offer'; right column a box with a single house and a small calendar labeled 'Home offer'. One arrow from Shared services to each. At the bottom: a box labeled 'Shared checkout' under the middle, receiving one arrow from 'Hotel offer' and one from 'Home offer'; and at the bottom right an older, slightly faded box labeled 'Legacy checkout' receiving one arrow from 'Home offer'. Exactly seven arrows.
alt: Travelers reach one front end with One Key loyalty and shared services above two distinct offers, hotel rooms and single homes; hotel and some home bookings use a shared checkout, other homes a legacy checkout.

visual_goal: Show the hotel supply contract: the OTA sells from its own copy, the hotel cannot reject confirmed bookings, delivery is ordered and acknowledged with email fallback.
prompt: A left-to-right swimlane illustration with three horizontal lanes labeled at the left edge from top to bottom: 'Channel manager', 'Travel platform', 'Traveler'. At the left, one arrow from the Channel manager lane down into the Travel platform lane, labeled 'rates and availability', landing on a small stored database copy icon labeled 'local copy'. Then one arrow from the Traveler lane, where an unlabeled generic traveler holds a phone, up into the Travel platform lane, labeled 'books'. Then one arrow from the Travel platform lane up to the Channel manager lane carrying a small envelope with a green check mark, labeled 'confirmed booking'. Then one arrow back down from the Channel manager lane to the Travel platform lane, labeled 'acknowledges'. At the far right, a small dashed orange arrow from the Travel platform lane to an envelope icon labeled 'email fallback'. Exactly five arrows.
alt: Swimlanes: the channel manager sends rates and availability into the platform's local copy; the traveler books against it; the platform sends an already confirmed booking that the channel manager acknowledges; repeated failure falls back to email.
